Black and white tiling
You don't like whiskey? Stay out.
No quick seating here

I've got to get something out from the outset: for god sake (okay mainly my sake), if you don't like whiskey don't go here and take up a seat that would better serve someone who is functionally literate and can read the sign on the door.

And here's why: 57 American Mashbill Bourbons, 14 Ryes, 44 Single malts, 13 Irish Whiskeys and 13 blended offerings, as well as a cocktail menu separated into prohibition and repeal era drinks. I ordered only off the established menu, but my bet is you can pretty much order any drink you want here with the knowledge that it will be excellent. They have beer, but there's no reason for that foolishness when there's enough whiskey to drown Delaware on hand.

With no reservations aside from walk-up and wait, we took our first round standing along the window counter. The counter and bar is open seating, so we snagged two end seats after circling like buzzards. The whole interior is solid, with tile floors and marble counters. The tiling blends well with the wood of the bar and leather of the seating areas, as if someone decided to stuff a speakeasy into the prep kitchen in a Newport mansion basement.

For the sake of organization, the spirits and dinner were:

Round 1 - Sazarac - A great looking rye drink, and perfect opening salvo to the evening. The sweetness of the sugar mixes well with the tang of bitters and the citrus of the lemon peel.

Round 2 - De Rigueur - Another rye, but you wouldn't know it from the color. The harsh rye blends well with the sweet aperol, and the citrus tang is balanced by the sugary honey. Looks like a 'ladies drink' but it'll knock you back.

Round 3 - Bakers 7 year - Skip desert, get a whiskey. I tried for the Evan Williams Single Barrel, but barring that reverted to a favorite. Bakers is harsh and I always enjoy it on the rocks, letting the water open up the sweeter flavors beneath the first bite.

And of course, drinking on an empty stomach is never a good idea. Village has a small menu, but pretty much just what you'd need, with a good range of prices. Consumed this evening was:

Appetizer - The Cheese Puffs are so dainty, and are a good dish for sharing. The cheese is melted right in to the dough, and they come oh so close to completely melting in your mouth.

Main course - Village Burger with onions and bleu cheese. For the quality, I would have paid a good bit more for this burger. Of course, all the toppings are a la carte, so if you have a big taste that evening, it could get pricey. The patty is enormous, but it was cooked perfectly as requested. The bleu cheese isn't chunky, but melted completely over the top, and the onions are piled on. By the last few bites, it only slightly resembled the original form, as it now looked like a juicy mash of bun and onion stuck together by cheese.

Village is, in every controllable way, a fantastic bar. The drinks are perfect, the staff is attentive (almost to a fault with regard to the bussers), and the atmosphere is brisk. I can't wait to head down here during the warmer months and score a table outside. With another fruity De Rigueur, of course.
